title: Finding the Distance of an Object (Ultrasonic Sensor)

content.aim: To measure the distance of an object using an ultrasonic sensor interfaced with an Arduino microcontroller.
objectives: To utilize an ultrasonic sensor to perform contactless measurements of physical quantities such as distance, level, position, and presence.
To understand the principles of high-frequency sound wave transmission and reflection.
To calculate distance by evaluating the time difference between sending and receiving a sound pulse.

theory.text:
Ultrasonic sensors measure physical quantities—such as distance, level, position, presence, and diameter—without requiring physical contact. The sensor consists of two main openings on its front: one housing a transmitter and the other a receiver. The transmitter emits a very high-frequency sound pulse into the air. This sound wave travels at a speed of approximately 341 meters per second in air. When the sound wave encounters an object, it is reflected back toward the sensor, where it is detected by the receiver.

By calculating the precise time difference between the transmission of the sound pulse and the reception of its echo, the distance to the reflecting object can be accurately determined. The mathematical relationship governing this is expressed as: Distance = Time * (speed of sound / 2). The formula divides the result by two because the measured time accounts for the round trip of the sound wave (traveling to the object and then bouncing back). content.discussion: The experiment successfully demonstrated the principles of contactless distance measurement using high-frequency sound waves. The ultrasonic sensor effectively utilized its transmitter to emit sound pulses and its receiver to detect the returning echoes. The Arduino efficiently captured the high-state duration of the echo pin using the pulseIn() function and computed the final distance using the speed of sound constant (0.034 cm/µs). This measurement technique provides a highly reliable foundation for applications like obstacle avoidance, position tracking, and level detection in automated systems.
content.conclusion: The distance of an object was successfully measured using an ultrasonic sensor and an Arduino Uno. The experiment reinforced the understanding of time-of-flight measurements and digital sensor interfacing.
